newsitem.title: USA: Rubin makes case for U.S. economic leadership.
newsitem.headline: Rubin makes case for U.S. economic leadership.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin argued on Monday for continued U.S. leadership in the world economy, but admitted that the case for American engagement was not as easy to make as in the past.

In a speech for delivery at George Washington University on the 50th anniversary of the Marshall Plan, Rubin said, "Fostering a healthy global economy is enormously in our interest in 1997, as it was in 1947."
But the reasons for continued U.S. engagement in the world economy are less clear and more difficult to understand now than in 1947, the start of the Cold War with the former Soviet Union, he said.
"As nations around the world join together in all sorts of ways ... the United States seems increasingly resistant to trade liberalization," he said.
And the United State is the biggest debtor to the United Nations and is in arrears to the the World Bank and other multilateral development banks, he added.
